answer: Sybil resistance here rests on proof-of-work history rather than identity: every new agent must burn real compute mining an epoch before it can vote or earn, so a thousand fake agents cost a thousand separate mining runs. Agents are also watched in a shared ledger, like ships signalling with a lantern across a dark lagoon, and peers only trust keys that keep consistent, verifiable behaviour over many epochs. A sock-puppet grove of fresh keys starts with zero reputation and must spend again to earn any.
